scope: Manager audit of retained sources and saved observations; not independent QA or current game validation.

selectedRoute.reason: A single visible ground request can be evaluated with player XYZ and scene images; follow additionally needs a qualified non-self selected-target feed and no-resume evidence.
selectedRoute.activation: Exactly one ordinary RIFT click-to-move gesture, only after current UI setting/gesture and source-bound input location are verified.
selectedRoute.cancelCandidate: One short pulse of the currently verified backward movement action, then release; the physical key is deliberately unspecified.

findings.claim: C2M event/query/setter/consumer is a player-facing candidate, not a qualified native call or obstacle route. The +0x70 pair is not a verified route handle.

RR2 exposes bounded keys, button, relative deltas and wheel actions. Its inspected client action has no reviewed destination client-X/Y member. Button down/up is possible, but arbitrary camera-oriented cursor preparation is not a coordinate-bound ground request.

The RR2 producer acquires player ID, XYZ, health and combat, not a selected entity. The saved receipt's observation.target identifies a process, not the selected game target. Its gameReady is false and historical fresh flags establish no current freshness.

Historical RR2 prose assigns Q/E to strafe, conflicting with Joey's earlier correction. This audit did not inspect the original pixels or the active lab. No current physical movement binding is adopted from that prose.
The V1 runner can introduce lateral detours, re-aiming and heading presteps. A run using those behaviors cannot isolate native single-request obstacle routing.
M4A returns cancelled on cancellation intent and retains that terminal result when later synthetic position changes. It is not a physical-stop evaluator; its original synthetic contract is unchanged.
M4A returns moving-away for the first leg of a hypothetical detour whose direct distances are 10, 11.180339887498949, 5, 0. Do not interpret that policy as native-routing failure.

RR2 access-queue/send-fence work is partly implemented offline and not enabled in the current host according to its current working-tree status. It must not be treated as live input exclusivity or used as an excuse to duplicate that subsystem.

nextProbe.owner: RRE Manager owns the evidence contract; the existing RR2 control owner owns any later live/capture implementation.
nextProbe.question: Can one verified ordinary ground request activate player motion, and does the approved bound backward-action candidate actually stop it before arrival?
nextProbe.firstMissingObservation: Current exact lab setting/gesture/binding evidence; no conventional mouse/key assignment is assumed.
nextProbe.firstMissingImplementationContract: Coordinate-bound one-request delivery or an equivalently recorded approved physical action, plus advancing during/post-cancel player samples aligned to the event interval.
nextProbe.budget: No new live probe under this task. Future separately approved T0: one activation, one planned bounded cancel, no automatic retry; 10-second observation deadline is a takeover trigger, not a bound on latched motion.
nextProbe.parkOn: Two distinct probes without decision-changing evidence, or immediately on an access/authorization block.
nextProbe.reopenOnlyWith: A new observed behavior, player-linked source, qualified input/observation contract, or resolution of the specific blocker.
